chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ahmad ibn 'Abdillah al-Qarawi from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Isma'il al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In the prayer of the two Eids,

he said: 'He takbir once, with which he initiates the prayer, then he recites Umm al-Kitab and a Surah, then he takbirs five times, making du'a between them, then he takbirs once and bows with it, then he stands and recites Umm al-Qur'an and a Surah; he recites in the first "Glory be to the name of your Lord, the Most High" and in the second "By the sun and its brightness", then he takbirs four times and makes du'a between them, then he bows with the fifth.'

key_terms.سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى: Glory be to the name of your Lord, the Most High (Surah Al-A'la)
key_terms.صَلاَةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: Prayer of the two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)
key_terms.وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا: By the sun and its brightness (Surah Ash-Shams)

ai.seo_question: What is the detailed method of performing the Eid prayer according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific ritual structure of the Eid prayer, emphasizing the distinct pattern of takbirs and qunut intervals that differentiate it from daily prayers. It highlights the Imam's role in establishing a unique liturgical rhythm, reinforcing the jurisprudential authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in shaping communal worship practices.
